title: Dynamic minimums and gradual burst attenuator for dedicated fleets
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduce a per-pool dynamic minimum capacity controller and a gradual burst attenuator to reduce oscillation, improve tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants, and provide clearer telemetry for min-capacity health.
description: Context and motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally suffer from oscillatory scale-downs followed by aggressive spikes when many tenants request short-lived bursts. This leads to preemptions, degraded tail latency, and higher unit cost due to excessive scale churn. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: (1) a Dynamic Min Capacity controller that computes and enforces a conservative minimum active slot count per pool based on recent utilization percentiles and commitment patterns, and (2) a Gradual Burst Attenuator that smooths tenant burst admissions over a short window instead of immediate spike admission. Goals: reduce scale oscillation, protect latency-sensitive tenants from noisy neighbors, and surface telemetry for min-capacity health and attenuator effectiveness.

review_comments: Miguel Alvarez: Can you explain why we chose the 95th percentile over 90th? The rationale in the RFC was leaning 90th in some workloads.
Priya Menon: Chose 95th to bias min-capacity slightly higher for latency-sensitive tenants; added config knob 'min_capacity_percentile' and documented tradeoffs in the RFC.
Zoe Chen: Unit test for the attenuator needs a deterministic clock; current test was flaky in CI.
Priya Menon: Switched tests to the injected Clock interface and added a deterministic time harness to the e2e.
Arjun Patel: Small nit: metric name 'dedicated_pool_min_capacity' should include pool label; otherwise querying per-pool is awkward.
Priya Menon: Updated metric to include pool_id label and added dashboard examples for aggregation by pool.
Miguel Alvarez: Approve after addressing tests and metric labeling.
Zoe Chen: Approved — verified e2e stability on staging cluster.
discussion_summary: Reviewers requested configurability (percentile knob), deterministic tests, and metric label changes. Author addressed feedback in follow-up commits; CI green. Approvals from Miguel and Zoe. Merged via squash.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'dynamic_minimums_v2' feature flag (default: off). Will enable in canary pool for 48h, monitor metrics: dedicated_pool_min_capacity, smoothed_utilization_p95, burst_admission_ramp_rate, and incident alerts for pool_degradation. Gradual rollout to EU and us-west, then all regions.
observability_notes: Added Prometheus metrics: dedicated_pool_min_capacity (gauge, labels: pool_id, region), smoothed_utilization_percentile (gauge), burst_attenuation_factor (gauge), burst_admissions_per_min (counter). Added dashboard panels and alert rules: MinCapacityDrop (when min capacity falls >30% over 10m) and BurstRampSpikes (when admission ramp > X/s).
upgrade_instructions: No breaking DB changes. Helm values added (autoscaler.minCapacity.enabled, autoscaler.burstAttenuator.windowSeconds, autoscaler.minCapacity.percentile). Operators must ensure feature flag is set in config; rollback simply disables feature flag.
tests_added: unit tests for percentile sampler, unit + integration tests for burst attenuator, e2e scenario that simulates 300 concurrent short bursts against a small pool; results included in PR artifacts.
notes: This PR reduces observed 99th tail latency regressions in staging from 420ms to 310ms under bursty synthetic load and reduced scale churn by ~18% in the same interval. Further tuning recommended per tenant to avoid over-reserving in low-util long-tail pools.
